title: Scalar extension square for cohomology of the universal derivation
statement:
Let $k\hookrightarrow K$ be an extension of fields [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], let $X$ be a smooth projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-projective-morphism], and put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$. Write $\Omega^0_{X/k}=\mathcal O_X$ and let $\Omega^1_{X/k}$ be the sheaf obtained by gluing the modules of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; write $d_X:\mathcal O_X\to\Omega^1_{X/k}$ for the universal $k$-linear derivation, and define $\Omega^p_{X_K/K},d_{X_K}$ similarly. For $p=0,1$ and every $q\geq0$, right-derived global sections in Zariski sheaves of $k$-vector spaces give the same $k$-vector spaces $H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/k})$ as ordinary module cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], and likewise over $K$. There are canonical $K$-linear isomorphisms $\beta^q_p:H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/k})\otimes_kK\cong H^q(X_K,\Omega^p_{X_K/K})$ with
$$\beta^q_1\circ(H^q(X,d_X)\otimes_k\mathrm{id}_K)=H^q(X_K,d_{X_K})\circ\beta^q_0.$$
The horizontal derivations and their cohomology maps are taken in sheaves of ground-field vector spaces, without imposing $\mathcal O_X$-linearity. No characteristic, connectedness or geometric integrality assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02KH, coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, separated-case Cech proof; Tag 01F1, cohomology-lemma-modules-abelian. Differential compatibility is the scalar formula d(a tensor lambda)=da tensor lambda and the universal differential base-change isomorphism of lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change; report.md spells out the Cech argument.

proof.text: Put $F_p=\Omega^p_{X/k}$ and $F'_p=\Omega^p_{X_K/K}$ for $p=0,1$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-module-abelian-cohomology] on the small Zariski site with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, and again with the constant ring sheaf $\underline k$. Sheaves of modules over $\underline k$ are exactly sheaves of $k$-vector spaces: a locally constant function acts piecewise, glued. An injective resolution is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so that node's $H^n$ is the cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology]. Both cohomologies therefore identify canonically with the cohomology of the same underlying abelian sheaf. These identifications are $k$-linear, since multiplication by each $a\in k$ is a module endomorphism in both categories and the cited comparison is natural. Repeat with $K,X_K$. This proves the scalar-forgetting assertion and permits computing $H^q(d_X)$ in vector-space sheaves.

By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper; by [def-weil-proper-morphism] it is separated. It is quasi-compact by the projectivity hypothesis. Choose a finite affine open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Each nonempty-tuple intersection $U_I$ is affine by iterating [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection]. For $g:X_K\to X$ put $V_i=g^{-1}U_i$. Inverse image preserves intersections and unions, so these form a cover and $V_I=g^{-1}U_I$. Apply [lem-pc-finite-affine-cech-intersection-base-change] with affine target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Z=U_I$: $V_I\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine, hence $V_I$ is affine. Empty intersections are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, separated-case affine cover; Tag 0BDX, lemma-affine-diagonal

proof.text: The sheaves $F_0,F_1$ and $F'_0,F'_1$ are quasi-coherent by their affine construction: on $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ they are $\widetilde A$ and $\widetilde{\Omega_{A/k}}$, which is exactly [pqf-def-coherent]; $F_1,F'_1$ are the sheaves $\Omega^1_{X/k},\Omega^1_{X_K/K}$ of [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] (same affine description). That node, with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}K$, gives the $\mathcal O_{X_K}$-linear isomorphism $c:g^*F_1\cong F'_1$, which on $U_K=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$ is the isomorphism $(A\otimes_kK)\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}\cong\Omega_{(A\otimes_kK)/K}$, $b\otimes da\mapsto b\,d(a\otimes1)$, of [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change]. For $p=0$ use $g^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_{X_K}$. Let $h_p:F_p\to g_*F'_p$ be the pullback unit followed by $g_*c$; on affine sections $h_0(a)=a\otimes1$ and $h_1(da)=d(a\otimes1)$, an additive map of sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 00RV, lemma-differentials-base-change, including its explicit universal derivation; affine gluing in the item

proof.text: Write $C_p^n=\prod_{I\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^{n+1}}\Gamma(U_I,F_p)$ and $C_p^{\prime n}=\prod_I\Gamma(V_I,F'_p)$, with differential $\delta=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{res}_j$. By [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] the modules have no positive cohomology on these affine intersections. Step 1 applied on each intersection gives the same vanishing for the underlying abelian sheaves and the vector-space sheaves. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-cech-edge-compatibility] supplies canonical isomorphisms $e_p^q:H^q(C_p)\cong H^q(X,F_p)$ and $e_p^{\prime q}:H^q(C'_p)\cong H^q(X_K,F'_p)$. The cited forgetting square identifies these with the module edges. Its additive naturality, applied to scalar multiplications, makes the edges linear, and applied to $d_X$ and $d_{X_K}$ gives $e_1H^q(D)=H^q(X,d_X)e_0$ and $e'_1H^q(D')=H^q(X_K,d_{X_K})e'_0$, where $D,D'$ apply the derivation to each coordinate. They are cochain maps because derivations commute with restriction and additive alternating sums.

Apply [lem-pc-flat-cech-base-change] with rings $k,K$, the separated structure morphism, the finite affine family $\mathcal U$, and the quasi-coherent module $F_p$. After the identifications $g^*F_p\cong F'_p$ of step 3, it gives a canonical $K$-linear chain isomorphism $\theta_p:C_p\otimes_kK\cong C'_p$. (Use the symmetry of tensor factors to match that node's $K\otimes_k C_p$ convention.) Its coordinate formula is $\theta_p(z\otimes\lambda)_I=\lambda\,h_p(z_I)$. Only the individual coefficient sheaves are used here as $\mathcal O_X$-modules; the map $D$ is a map of complexes of $k$-vector spaces.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, relation between Cech complexes; Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change

proof.text: The two chain maps from $C_0\otimes_kK$ to $C'_1$ agree. Indeed, on a pure tensor $z\otimes\lambda$ and a tuple $I$ with coordinate $a=z_I$, one has $D'\theta_0(z\otimes\lambda)_I=d_{X_K}(\lambda(a\otimes1))=\lambda\,d_{X_K}(a\otimes1)=\theta_1(Dz\otimes\lambda)_I$. The middle equality is the Leibniz rule and $d_{X_K}(\lambda)=0$ from [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; the last equality is precisely the formula of [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change]. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove $D'\theta_0=\theta_1(D\otimes1)$ in every degree.

source.place: Tag 00RV, lemma-differentials-base-change, formula for the base-changed derivation

proof.text: By [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact], tensoring with $K$ is exact. Applied to the kernel, image and quotient defining $H^q(C_p)$, exactness gives the canonical isomorphism $t_p:H^q(C_p)\otimes_kK\cong H^q(C_p\otimes_kK)$ with $t_p([z]\otimes\lambda)=[z\otimes\lambda]$. This works for the possibly unbounded Cech complex, since only the two adjacent differentials enter a fixed cohomology group. The displayed formula also proves naturality: both composites for a cochain map $f$ send $[z]\otimes\lambda$ to $[f(z)\otimes\lambda]$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, exact tensor after the separated-case Cech calculation

proof.text: Define $\beta_p^q=e_p^{\prime q}\,H^q(\theta_p)\,t_p\,((e_p^q)^{-1}\otimes1)$. Every factor is $K$-linear and invertible. To check canonicity, the inverse-image functor on opens $U\mapsto g^{-1}U$ preserves the final open, tuple intersections and covers. Apply the site-change square of [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-cech-edge-compatibility] to $h_p:F_p\to g_*F'_p$. All its acyclicity hypotheses were checked in step 4. Its cochain map is $z\mapsto\theta_p(z\otimes1)$ by step 5; hence $\beta_p^q(x\otimes\lambda)=\lambda\,h_{p,H}^q(x)$, where $h_{p,H}^q$ is the canonical cohomology pullback of $h_p$. This formula characterizes $\beta_p^q$ independently of the chosen affine cover and agrees, under the cited forgetting square, with ordinary scalar base change on module cohomology.

source.place: Tag 03AX, lemma-cech-cohomology, the restriction and coefficient augmentations; Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree

proof.text: Finally step 6 gives $H^q(D')H^q(\theta_0)=H^q(\theta_1)H^q(D\otimes1)$. Insert the naturality $H^q(D\otimes1)t_0=t_1(H^q(D)\otimes1)$ from step 7 and the two edge identities of step 4 into the definition of $\beta_p^q$. The result is $H^q(X_K,d_{X_K})\beta_0^q=\beta_1^q(H^q(X,d_X)\otimes1)$, as asserted. Equivalently, on a cycle representative $z$ both paths send $e_0^q([z])\otimes\lambda$ to $e_1^{\prime q}([\theta_1(Dz\otimes\lambda)])$. Pure tensors generate the source, so this verifies the whole square.
